input: root is absent or a finite acyclic binary tree with n distinct node objects, no shared child nodes, safe-integer values, and a safe-integer target. Every node is an ordinary mutable object with writable val, left and right data fields. Each child is another node or None in Python/null in JavaScript. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. Python integers are plain int values, excluding bool; node identity keys, when used, are opaque id values.
return: Original root after repeatedly removing all target-valued leaves until stable, or the absent value if the root is eventually removed. Non-target leaves and all remaining node identities are preserved.
mutation_aliasing: Intentionally replaces child links with absent values when pruned. Caller aliases observe every link change; node values are never changed and detached objects are not destroyed. A removed root is reported only by the returned absent value, not by mutating the caller variable. No new nodes are created; the Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Only exact safe-integer equality on values/target is needed; traversal indices and storage counts are bounded by n. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(h + 1) auxiliary space for original height h. The explicit two-phase postorder stack has at most a constant number of records per active ancestor; after children are processed, a single leaf check handles all cascading removals. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.
